walkthroughs.body_html: Coccolithophores and pteropods form the base of many marine food webs. As CO2 dissolves and aragonite saturation falls, their calcium carbonate plates dissolve and reproduction is impaired. Reduced plankton biomass cascades up to krill, herring, mackerel and ultimately whales, seabirds and people.

Acidification combines with warming, deoxygenation and overfishing to threaten over 3 billion people who rely on fish for protein. Shellfish industries in the Pacific Northwest have already shifted hatcheries to buffered water. Subsistence fisheries in Pacific islands and Africa face the largest food security risks despite contributing least to emissions.

The primary solution is cutting CO2 emissions; secondary measures include reducing local pollution, creating marine protected areas, supporting reef restoration via coral gardening, and breeding more resilient shellfish strains. International agreements like the UN High Seas Treaty (2023) aim to protect 30 percent of oceans by 2030.
